Dozens of loud taps hit wet stone in quick succession as a sinuously segmented crustacean rushes across the rocky coast under the gray 
light of rain laden clouds. Long antennae whip through the salty air, catching the musty scent of a gharril clutch on the cliffs above. 
Now sensing easy prey, the crustacean speeds up the near vertical outcropping, closing in quickly as its multitude of pronged claws fi nd 
easy purchase on the stone. Without an uttered sound it crests the cliff face and strikes in an explosion of violence. Eviscerated salty 
gore and broken shell stream down the stone as the nicalliath feasts. Th ese far ranging predators dominate most environments on the 
island, to such a point that they must constantly stay on the move, lest their hunting grounds grow devoid of prey.

Aggressive Ambusher Th e nicalliath has Advantage on attack 
rolls against any creature it has Surprised.
Multiattack Th e nicalliath makes three attacks, it can use its 
Slicing Appendages, Viciously Rend or Segmented Constriction 
attacks in any combination.
Slicing Appendages Melee Attack Roll: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one 
target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage. 
Viciously Rend Melee Attack Roll: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. 
Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) Piercing damage. If target is a Medium or smaller 
creature and the nicalliath moved 20+ ft. straight toward it 
immediately before the hit, the target takes an addition 7 (2d6) 
damage and has the Prone condition.
Segmented Constriction Melee Attack Roll: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., 
one target creature. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. If the 
target is Medium or smaller creature, it is Grappled (Escape DC 
16). Th e Nicalliath can only grapple one creature at a time, and 
until this grapple ends, the nicalliath can Viciously Rend only 
the grappled creature.
Amphibious Th e nicalliath can breathe both air and water.
Sensitive Antennae Th e nicalliath has Advantage on Wisdom 
(Perception) checks and Wisdom (Survival) checks that rely on 
smell, and can scent creatures through both water and air.
Lethal Chitin Th e nicalliath’s attacks score a Critical hit on a 19 or a 
20. If the nicalliath scores a Critical hit on a creature, the creature’s 
max Hit Points are reduced by 1d6. Th is reduction lasts until the 
target fi nishes a Long Rest. If the target’s Hit Point maximum is 
reduced to 0, the target dies.
Senses Darkvision 60 ft., Tremorsense 60 ft., passive Perception 14
Challenge 6 (XP 2,300; PB 3)
Aggressive Instinct (1/Day) To single minded and aggressive to realize 
when its suffering a mortal wound, the crustacean lashes out.
Reaction - Trigger: When the nicalliath has reached 0 hit points.
Response - Constitution Saving Th row: DC 14, the nicalliath. Success: In 
its death throes, it spasms aggressively and attempts to move and 
make a single melee attack roll of its choice towards the nearest 
enemy. Afterwards, the nicalliath collapses, slain.
Skills Perception +5, Stealth +7
Immunities Prone
Resistances Acid, Poison, Slashing
Encountering Capable of hunting within nearly every 
environment of Sol’Kesh, the nicalliath is a potential threat 
anywhere, but is rarely found out in the heat of the sun or the 
cold heights. As the crustacean must keep its body fairly moist, 
it prefers to hunt down isolated beasts during rainstorms or in 
the cool air before the light of dawn. During the day it can be 
found resting under stone or within the mud of river banks.
Mindless Aggression Th e nicalliath can move up to its speed 
toward a hostile creature it can smell.
Tendrils drag behind the females, leaving trails of 
pheromones for males to follow during the mating 
seasons. As these lone crustaceans often spend months 
without seeing another of their kind
Long antennae taste the air for nearby 
prey or the subtle hints of fresh air in 
the depths of the Umbrawells
The nicalliath often rushes heedlessly into prey, slamming 
its bladed head into flesh and shell alike as each forward 
facing edge is adapted to pierce and ravage. Against more 
nimble prey, the crustacean has been known to break its 
sharp carapace upon stone and trees when it misses
Dozens of legs cascade down the 
creatures centipede-like body, ranging 
from two claw digits to single spearing 
points. With this array of limbs, the 
crustacean is able to grip and pierce 
most surfaces from stone to wood, 
leaving very few environments that the 
creature cannot traverse
